I will keep this year simple and steady. In Quzhou County, I would stay with the wheat-maize rotation because I know it well, the land suits it, and it spreads my income across the year. At my age, I would not chase complicated crops that need more labor, more market judgment, or finer management. I would carry my winter wheat through spring with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations at the key stages, and only spray when I see a real problem. After wheat harvest, I would plant summer maize right away to hold yield and make full use of the season. I would use improved seed, not the cheapest traditional seed, because I want stable output and easier management. For tillage, I would mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical, familiar, and lighter than deep ploughing every time. I would keep fertilizer and water at moderate levels: enough to protect yield, but not excessive, because inputs are expensive and too much nitrogen can cause trouble. My plan is not to maximize risk or chase the highest possible yield; it is to get a reliable harvest I can manage myself.
